The surface effects applied by Nature's Vengeance are:
 Fire: Apply Burning for 2 turns. Deals the first tick of 1d4Fire damage immediately.
Caustic Brine: Apply Caustic Brine for 2 turns. Deals the first tick of 1d4Acid damage immediately.
Simple Toxin: Apply Poisoned for 2 turns.
Acid: Apply Acid for 2 turns.

name: Belm
title: Belm
description: Belm is a very rare +2 Scimitar. It grants the Whirlwind Attack and Perfectly Balanced Strike weapon actions.
quote: Faded but still legible, the mark of a Kara-Turan forgemaster adorns the pommel of this exquisite sword. Light as a robin's wing, quick as a gnomish wit, this weapon has unseamed many foes - and will continue to, in the correct hands.
properties: Feint an attack to possibly throw your opponent Off Balance. ( Recharge: Short rest.)
Slash at your target's vital points to make it Bleed. ( Recharge: Short rest.)
Send Belm snaking out with an adder's speed, the very exemplar of swiftness embodied in steel. ( Recharge: Per turn.)

where_to_find: Elerrathin's Home X: -210 Y: -50: in an opulent chest in the basement
notes: The chest containing this weapon is in a room behind a locked ( DC 18 Sleight of Hand Check) bookcase.

This weapon was originally found in Baldur's Gate 2, and is considered one of the best weapons in that game, as it allows the wielder to make one more attack with the weapon held in the main-hand per round.

Perfectly Balanced Strike is a variation of Dueller's Enthusiasm, allowing the wielder to make an "offhand-like" attack with Belm while it is in their main hand. The difference is that there are no restrictions on Belm's variation – shields and offhand weapons do not disable the weapon action.

When Belm is equipped in the offhand, Perfectly Balanced Strike functions as an additional main-hand weapon attack. This attack uses all the stats and on-hit effects of the equipped main-hand weapon, including adding the wielder's ability modifier to the damage without the need of Two-Weapon Fighting. This effect mimics how additional attacks worked in Baldur's Gate 1 and 2 which used AD&D (i.e., 2e) rules.
Other than the once-per-Short Rest recharge time, this action is equivalent to the Hunter version. Refer there for more detailed notes.

quote: The tibia of a storm giant was ground and chiselled and reworked till it became this helm. The wearer can actually smell summer tempest clouds like maroon-dark dread while wearing the helm.

notes:
For the version of Menacing Attack (Melee) granted by this item:
The DC is determined by the same method as other manoeuvres.
The bonus damage is not equal to a Superiority Die, as would be the case for a regular Menacing Attack; it is instead equal to the wearer's proficiency bonus.
Unlike any of the manoeuvres granted by the Battle Master subclass, the Menacing Attack granted by this helmet recharges per turn.

As with other manoeuvres, it uses a weapon attack roll which qualifies for Extra Attack. This makes it an attractive option for use at the beginning of every combat round for melee combatants with Extra Attack and level 11+ fighters in particular.
This weapon action is usable even if the wielder is not proficient with their equipped melee weapon.
The 2-8 Psychic damage mentioned in the in-game tooltip of Fury in the Marrow is, specifically, 2d4 Psychic damage.
bugs: Hostile creatures that succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against Fury In The Marrow receive no damage instead of half damage.

name: Broodmother's Revenge
title: Broodmother's Revenge
description: The Broodmother's Revenge is an uncommon Amulet. It coats the wearer's weapon in poison for 2 turns whenever they are healed.
quote: Each of this amulet's jewels shines like a viper's eyes.
properties: Whenever the wearer is healed, their weapon becomes coated in magic and deals an additional 1d6Poison damage.
where_to_find: Inner Sanctum X: -461 Y: -22: Carried by Kagha in the Emerald Grove
High Hall X: 235 Y: 44: On a table of goods, owned by Koll
notes: This item synergizes well with the Derivation Cloak and Poisoner's Gloves, especially when used by characters with high attack modifiers or multiple attacks per round.

It is possible to obtain this item while keeping Kagha alive and friendly within the grove. During the confrontation with Kagha for the quest Investigate Kagha, she must be convinced to side with the party. After celebrating with the tieflings in camp after defeating the goblin leaders, Kagha will be standing alone, along the pathway entering the grove. Attacking her and knocking her out with Toggle Non-Lethal Attacks makes her lootable yet keeps her alive. Following a long rest, Kagha will be awake again and upset, but non-hostile. Trading with her via bartering can bring her relationship with the party back into good standing.
Venomous Revenge applies to both melee and ranged weapons, but, as with all poison coatings, its effect does not work when a weapon is Thrown.
The effect is triggered even with full health or when being picked up from a Downed state.

The effect is triggered by:
being targeted by any healing spell, like Healing Word.
consuming any healing items, like a Potion of Healing, a Goodberry, or a Raspberry.
all equipment with continuous regeneration effects: the Helm of Balduran and Ring of Regeneration.
healing effects from the Derivation Cloak and Armour of Landfall.

The effect is not triggered by:
Most self-healing effects from equipment: Shattered Flail, Sword of Chaos, Woe, Robe of the Weave, Psionic Ward Armour, Vest of Soul Rejuvenation, Circlet of Mental Anguish, or Wapira's Crown.
Healing from Transfuse Health.

This effect interacts in the following ways with dipping and coatings:
The effect overwrites Dipped in Fire and vice versa.
The effect does not trigger for an already coated weapon (e.g. Drow Poison).
Coatings overwrite the effect.

As Tenacity deals weapon damage even if an attack misses, it can trigger many on-hit effects from equipment. For example, from the Gloves of Power, the Callous Glow Ring, weapon coatings, or any infusion from the Ring of Elemental Infusion.
This action does not count as an attack for the purposes of Extra Attack and requires the wielder's full Action.
bugs: As Horde Breaker (Melee) rolls invisible, zero-damage weapon attacks against all enemies in the Horde Breaker area of effect, Tenacity can be prompted to trigger against them even if the first attack hits. It is therefore possible to score 2 hits in one attack: the full attack against the original Horde Breaker target and a Tenacity hit against another target.

Since this attack does not involve an attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include:
 Arcane Synergy
Great Weapon Master: All In
Hunter's Mark
Wrath
Despite the tooltip warning, Large and bigger sized targets are pushed back.

The combat log erroneously shows the formula for spell save DC in the saving throw, often showing a calculation that does not add up to the final DC. The actual value is calculated using weapon action DC.

bugs:
When dual-wielding a flail or morningstar with a non-Tenacity weapon using the Dual Wielder feat, Tenacity can be triggered by missing an attack with the non-Tenacity weapon, dealing Bludgeoning damage regardless of the weapon used.

title: Derivation Cloak
description: Derivation Cloak is a rare Cloak which heals the wearer for 1d4 Hit Points when they Poison a foe.

properties: When you Poison a foe, heal yourself for 1d4Hit Points.
where_to_find: Moonrise Towers X: -132 Y: -175: In a heavy chest in Balthazar's chambers on the First Floor
notes:
There are four Poisoned conditions reusing the same icon, which can be confusing. The most general one is Poisoned, and it's the only one considered by this passive. That means there will be no healing via the following similar conditions:
 Poisoned (Basic Poison) condition caused by a weapon coated in Basic Poison. But the same item when thrown generates a Poison Cloud, which can cause the correct Poisoned condition, triggering this passive.
Poisoned (Suspicious Poison) condition caused by drinking or throwing Suspicious Poison.
Poisoned (Spider Meat) condition caused by consuming Spider meat.
This passive has great synergy when combined with Poisoner's Gloves and Broodmother's Revenge. Every attack can cause Poisoned, healing the character and refreshing the poison coating.

The player character can only purchase Dolor Amarus from the Echo of Abazigal if they accept becoming an Unholy Assassin of Bhaal. However, it can also be acquired through an exploit – see notes on the Echo of Abazigal page for details.

Dolor Amarus applies to all weapon attacks while a weapon with the feature is equipped, and it can be activated multiple times if multiple weapons with the passive are equipped. For example, if both Dolor Amarus daggers are equipped – or one dagger and the Vicious Battleaxe on a character with Dual Wielder – together with the Vicious Shortbow, when the wielder lands a critical hit, then +21 damage will be added, instead of +7.
Dolor Amarus also stacks on multiple damage riders, which could potentially lead to massive bonuses from different damage sources.
The name dolor amarus is Latin for "harsh suffering" or "bitter sorrow".

Lethal Weapon does not bypass immunity to Bludgeoning, only resistance.

Lethal Weapon applies to Unarmed Strikes made while the weapon is equipped. Most characters cannot make Unarmed Strikes while a melee weapon is equipped in their main hand, but monks who are level 5 or higher can use Stunning Strike (Unarmed) or Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike as a Bonus Action and gain this benefit.

Lethal Weapon also causes other sources of Bludgeoning damage from a character with the weapon equipped to ignore resistance. For example, a dual-wielded Bludgeoning damage weapon in melee, the Dwarven Thrower being thrown, or the spell Ice Storm.

bugs:
The reader is advised that Battlemage's Power appears to have some of the most complex and unintuitive behaviour in the game, making it difficult to distinguish what is actually a bug.
Any damage dealt while wielding a normal, non-permanent Flame Blade in the main hand triggers Battlemage's Power. The damage can be from any source such as weapon attacks, spell damage (including each dart from Magic Missile and each blast from Eldritch Blast), or even damage from status effects like Burning. Battlemage's Power does not trigger if the conjured weapons are in the off-hand, even if attacking with the conjured weapon. This only works with a normal, temporary Flame Blade summoned by the corresponding spell and not with a permanent Flame Blade acquired through hireling exploit. This effect also used to work while wielding a Shadow Blade in the main hand, but this was removed in a hotfix after Patch 8.

Battlemage's Power does not function with the Mephistopheles Tiefling version of Flame Blade, as this version has a different condition applied to it which is not listed in the ArcaneAcuityGlovesCondition() .khn script.
Throwing Healing Potions and Grenades triggers Battlemage's Power, even without hitting any target.

Reaction Smites provide acuity if and only if the triggering attack provided acuity. If the source attack does trigger Battlemage's Power, reaction smite triggers them a second time, for a total of +4 Acuity.

All of the following provide Acuity:
Persistent AoE spell effects like Cloudkill and Wall of Fire
Every status in the game which deals damage attributed to the wearer triggers Battlemage's Power. For example, Burning and Electrocuted.
Fall damage caused by the wearer
Some miscellaneous effects like the Holy Lance Helm

Retaliation effects do not trigger Battlemage's Power.
This includes onHit effects such as Armour of Agathys and Fire Shield; onDamage effects such as Fleshmelter Cloak; and onMiss effects such as Shield of Scorching Reprisal.

Battlemage's Power is meant to have a OncePerAttack restriction, meaning they should only provide Acuity once per damaging event. However, the OncePerAttack limit gets reset every time the player character performs any effect which targets any in-game entity, whether that entity is an enemy, an ally, or the wearer themself.
This includes regular attacks as well as self-target abilities like Dash and Rage.

This also includes effects the game considers an "attack" (due to underlying code) such as: using the Perform action (including in combat), speaking with the Sentient Amulet (including in combat), targeting someone with the ability check version of Bend Luck, and provoking an attack of opportunity (though if the wearer takes damage from it, they lose 2 Acuity).
Explosions also reset the gloves' once per attack limit. This includes the AOE "explosions" from Hamarhraft and Luminous Armour as well as grenades like Alchemist's Fire and Caustic Bulb.

temporary hit points are included in the calculation of total hit points required to activate Grit, including with the below listed bug.

notes: After a creature is killed, the Executioner critical hit can be set to 'Ask' or disabled entirely in the Reactions tab, allowing it to be saved for later. Using it does not consume a Reaction resource.
The automatic critical hit from Executioner can be applied to every target hit by a single AOE attack, such as Whirlwind Attack or Razor Gale.
bugs: Despite the tooltip suggesting otherwise, Executioner only applies to weapon attack rolls.

When using weapon specific abilities that impose a saving throw such as Pushing Attack (Melee) and Lacerate, Executioner attempts to apply its 'Natural 20' effect to the enemy's saving throw as well as the character's attack. This creates a risk of wasting the Executioner condition to help the enemy.

If the Executioner reaction is set to 'Automatic': the game forces the character's attack roll to a 20 (a Critical Hit) but also forces the target’s Saving Throw to a 20. This grants the enemy a high probability of resisting the secondary effect (e.g., they take the damage but are not pushed).
If the Executioner reaction is set to 'Ask': The game triggers two separate prompts:
First Prompt: asks to turn the character's attack roll into a 20. (Recommend: Yes)

Second Prompt: asks to turn the enemy's Saving Throw into a 20. (Recommend: No)
If the character accepts the second prompt, the Executioner condition is consumed, and the enemy receives a large bonus to their save.
Note: While Saving Throws do not technically 'critically succeed' on a 20, the high roll often results in the enemy resisting the effect.

name: Loviatar's Scourge
title: Loviatar's Scourge
description: Loviatar's Scourge is an uncommon Mace that grants the wielder resistance to Necrotic damage. It also deals additional Necrotic damage to all nearby creatures, including the wielder.
quote: More club than scourge, this weapon has a serrated edge made for drawing long, shallow cuts.
properties: Grants Resistance to Necrotic damage. Deals an additional 1d6NecroticDRS damage to nearby targets, including the wielder.

where_to_find: Shattered Sanctum X: 338 Y: -21: Carried by Abdirak
notes: If this mace is purchased from Abdirak through his barter screen, it transfers back to him automatically when he needs to use it.
The area of effect is centred on the creature that is hit, and the radius is 2 m (7 ft).
Due to the resistance granted by this passive, the wielder takes only 0~3Necrotic damage (fractional damage is rounded down). However, nearby allies take full damage.
Helldusk Armour effectively negates all Necrotic damage otherwise inflicted upon the wielder by this passive.

Attacks which deal multiple instances of damage, such as the various smite spells or Booming Blade, trigger multiple instances of Willing Whip.
Similarly, weapon attacks that target multiple creatures, such as Tiger's Bloodlust, cause this passive to activate separately on each successful attack, potentially causing the wielder and all nearby creatures to take significant damage.
This feature is particularly useful against groupings of low-hit-point enemies that may otherwise have many opportunities to score critical hits against the party.

If Lae'zel is in the party while fighting the murder of Shadow-Cursed Ravens on the Ruined Battlefield in Act Two at X: 30 Y: 114, the area of effect damage from this passive may easily earn the Soldier's Pentacrush Inspiration, while taking little to no damage in the process.
bugs: Some damage riders like Lightning Charges and Callous Glow (from Callous Glow Ring) are added both to regular attacks and to the Willing Whip effect, so they also hurt the mace wielder.

Creatures close to the one struck by this weapon take damage every time, but those on the border of its AoE radius sometimes do not. This is especially noticeable with wide area attacks, such as Slashing Flourish (Melee).

When dual-wielding Loviatar's Scourge with a flail or morningstar using the Dual Wielder feat, Tenacity can be triggered by missing an attack with the mace, dealing Bludgeoning damage and triggering Willing Whip.

notes: The Moonlantern carried by Kar'niss contains a foul-mouthed pixie Dolly Dolly Dolly who wants out. If freed using Inspect Moonlantern, she grants the party a Pixie Blessing.
If Dolly is freed, her Moonlantern remains in the inventory of the character who freed her, but its inventory icon changes to a broken version and the lantern cannot be equipped anymore.
If Kar'niss arrives at Moonrise Towers with the lantern (whether he escorted the party or not), Dolly dies inside it.

If Kar'niss is killed at the ambush and the lantern is taken by the Harpers, the party can follow them back to Last Light Inn. There Isobel gives the party the same Moonlantern with Dolly Dolly Dolly alive inside; she can be freed and the Pixie Blessing may then still be obtained.

Switching to ranged weapons while having a Moonlantern equipped retains the Moonshield effect but removes the illumination, allowing darkness-requiring effects such as Covert Critical and Shadow Step to be safely used within the Shadow-Cursed Lands.

notes:
Elemental Augmentation functions by checking the cantrip being cast for a specific DamageType flag (such as Fire or Lightning) rather than the actual damage type listed for the cantrip or the damage type dealt when hitting a target. This means that 'added' damage – such as that from Lightning Charges – does not trigger the necklace's effect, because these external bonuses lack the necessary flags. Consequently, the necklace only works with cantrips which natively deal the correct damage types, and does not work with cantrips which erroneously lack a DamageType flag, like Booming Blade.
There are no cantrips in the game with a DamageType of Thunder.

Elemental Augmentation stacks with the Elemental Affinity: Damage feature for most Draconic Bloodline Sorcerers (except for those with green dragon ancestry, which increases Poison damage). In this case, the wearer's Charisma modifier is added to the damage of the relevant cantrips twice.

When multiclassing, Elemental Augmentation uses the spellcasting ability modifier of the last class added, not necessarily the spellcasting ability of the class which granted the cantrip.
The minimum additional damage is 1, even if the character's spellcasting ability modifier is less than 1.
Hellflame Cleave deals two instances of damage, which both receive the bonus damage from Elemental Augmentation.
The following cantrips receive bonus damage from Elemental Augmentation:

If the player does not have the Orphic Hammer on hand and they choose side with Orpheus, Raphael, if still alive, comes to the Astral Plane to either hand it over to the party after signing a deal or return it to the party if the deal was signed. Refusing the deal, attacking him or not having the Orphic Hammer if Raphael is dead causes an instant Game Over.

This is the only action in the game able to destroy the Infernal Crystals keeping Hope imprisoned.
Unshackling Strike does not free Orpheus, instead, the Infernal Crystals (not the Minor Orb of Domination) need to be struck with a regular attack while wielding the Orphic Hammer.
Unshackling Strike uses a melee weapon attack roll, meaning that using it against a friendly character with high Armor Class is likely to result in a miss.

The icon for this action is reminiscent of the Dispel Magic icons in Baldur's Gate 1 and 2, and it is in fact labelled Spell_Abjuration_DispelMagic within the game files. However, according to Swen Vincke, Dispel Magic was cut content for Baldur's Gate 3. He relates how Baldur's Gate 3 devs tried to make D&D's Dispel Magic work for a long time, but ultimately abandoned it: "it would've doubled the size of the game."

name: Phalar Aluve
title: Phalar Aluve
description: Phalar Aluve is a rare +1 Longsword that can be made to Sing or Shriek, granting nearby allies or enemies a bonus to Attack Rolls or damage rolls, depending on the choice.
properties: The sword hums in anticipation, ready to Sing or Shriek (see bugs on their respective pages). ( Recharge: Short rest.)
Slash at your target's vital points to make it Bleed. ( Recharge: Short rest.)
Make a non-lethal attack against an enemy and possibly Daze them. ( Recharge: Short rest.)
Charge forward and attack the first enemy in your way, possibly pushing them Off Balance. ( Recharge: Short rest.)
where_to_find: Underdark X: 116 Y: -192: Embedded inside a rock
notes:
The sword can be freed in these ways:
Passing a DC 15 Strength Check to yank it from the stone.
Passing a DC 15 Religion Check to learn how to release the magic holding it in place. Clerics of Lolth have advantage on this check.

Paladins can pass a DC 10 Religion Check (with Advantage) to consider what the appropriate ritual for releasing the sword is. If successful, they can perform the ritual or use their oath to prove their worth ( DC 10 Charisma Check).
Clerics of Eilistraee can release the sword without needing an ability check.

Spilling blood on the sword outside dialogue also releases it. It is possible to make one party member hit another, or perform a Blood Sacrifice if a party member has the Ritual Dagger, to cover the sword in a Blood surface. It is also possible throw a dead body on the sword. This will make it light up, so it can be pulled out without any ability check.
Longswords do not normally have the Finesse property; Phalar Aluve is special in this regard. The only other example is Larethian's Wrath.
Phalar Aluve is Drow language. Phalar means 'battle-marker' or 'grave', and Aluve means 'I/we leave you'.

Obtaining the sword grants the inspiration Last Rites of the Dark Dancer for party members with the Acolyte background, unless the sword was obtained through the dialogue option of a paladin using the strength of their oath.

Although it has a distinctive appearance during the cutscene for its retrieval, when equipped this sword has an appearance similar to that of a Longsword +1, save for its blade, hilt and pommel, which are gold instead of polished steel.

name: Ring of Elemental Infusion
title: Ring of Elemental Infusion
description: The Ring of Elemental Infusion is an uncommon Ring that infuses your weapon with the element of your spells or cantrips, dealing additional damage.
quote: The mysterious gem set in this ring seems to change hues whenever you aren't looking.
properties:
When you deal Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage using a Spell or a Cantrip, that element infuses your weapon.
Until the end of your next turn, you deal an additional 1d4 damage of that element on your first successful weapon attack.
where_to_find: Crèche Y'llek X: 1303 Y: -798: Worn by Gish Umr'a'ac in the southern section of the Infirmary
notes: Elemental Infusion can apply its damage bonus multiple times to a single weapon attack.

The individual elemental damage boost conditions all share the same StackID with each other, meaning only one may be active on a character at a time. However, the conditions also use a StackType of Overwrite, meaning the last condition applied from the passive is the condition that will actually affect the wearer's next weapon attack. Due to the way the passive is written, this causes a priority effect where the conditions follow this order of priority (with the later conditions overwriting the earlier conditions):
 Acid Infusion < Cold Infusion < Fire Infusion < Lightning Infusion < Thunder Infusion
This means that if a character attacks an enemy with a spell that deals primarily Fire damage, but is also dealing bonus Thunder damage, the character will be left with Thunder Infusion.

properties: Chance to inflict upon the target a 1d4 penalty to Attack Rolls and Saving Throws. If the attacker still has 50% or more hit points, they take 1d6Piercing themselves.

where_to_find: Shattered Sanctum X: 338 Y: -26: on the table next to Abdirak
notes: The Bane condition applied by this weapon is the same as the Bane spell and does not stack.
Because of the bug listed below, the Battle Master Fighter's Sweeping Attack applies this debuff to every target within the cone's area of effect, hit or miss.

Many situations increase the self-damage dealt by this passive feature:
The Savage Attacker feat results in secondary damage being re-rolled higher.
A critical hit with this axe doubles the self-damage.
Some damage riders such as Lightning Charges, radiant damage from the Callous Glow Ring and Psionic Overload increase the self-damage.

Effects which reduce incoming piercing damage reduce the self-inflicted damage.
However, as the self-damage is classified as magical, Heavy Armour Master damage reduction does not apply.
If at 50% health or higher, the wielder suffers self-damage even if the target dies from the axe blow.
bugs: While the item description says 'chance,' Bane is always inflicted on a hit.
If the wielder of this axe is at 50% health or higher and they use Non-Lethal Damage to knock out an enemy with it, they will also be knocked out, even if at full HP.

The actual distance of Darkvision often depends on the creature that has this feature. The values above are the default for playable races.

When a hiding creature enters the line of sight of a creature with darkvision, and is within the range of darkvision:
Being Lightly Obscured counts as being under Clear Area instead.

name: Sentient Amulet (Rare)
title: Sentient Amulet (Rare)
description: Sentient Amulet is a rare Amulet that allows the wearer to cast Shatter once per Short Rest (with a drawback) and Ki Restoration (Lesser) once per Long Rest.
quote: Sun-graced warmth radiates from both the pendant and its chain. Somehow, even a brief glance of it brings a smile to your face.
properties: Cast as a level 2 spell ( Recharge: Short rest.)
Speak with the consciousness lingering inside the Sentient Amulet.
Using the spiritual energy in the amulet, you restore 2 Ki Points. ( Recharge: Long rest.)

The amulet's spirit lingers, making everything seem a little more vibrant. Must succeed a Wisdom Saving Throw (DC 10/15/20, see notes) when using the amulet's power, or become Hysterical (equivalent in effect to Tasha's Hideous Laughter with a duration of 1 turn).
where_to_find: Abandoned Refuge X: -624 Y: 224: In a locked Adamantine Chest on the island with the broken structure near the Lava Elemental in Grymforge
notes: Picking up the amulet triggers a conversation in which the amulet tries to get party member to surrender to a fit of laughter. This is a hint at the curse the amulet bears. Once the conversation is over, the quest Help the Cursed Monk is received.
The amulet is voiced by John O'Mahony.
Wisdom Saving Throws are only required when using this amulet to cast Shatter. Using the Ki Restoration (Lesser) ability does not prompt a Wisdom save.

The default Wisdom Saving Throw for Hysterical is a DC 10. However, after succeeding the Saving Throw at least three times and upon either equipping the amulet or leaving camp (whichever happens first), a special cutscene plays where passing a DC 10 Wisdom Saving Throw to resist the curse is necessary. If failed, the Hysterical DC is increased to 15. If the Wisdom Saving Throw for Hysterical is succeeded a further three times (and then equipping the amulet or leaving camp again), a similar cutscene plays whereby failing a DC 15 Wisdom Saving Throw increases the Hysterical DC to 20. After this, no additional cutscenes will occur.

Depending on the outcome of the Help the Spirit of the Amulet quest in Act Three, the party may receive a version of this amulet that is visually identical but missing all of its special properties (UID: UNI_WYR_MonkAmulet_NoGhost / UUID: 14a6da9a-6689-4c70-96a1-d03319ba3278). Alternatively, the player may receive the Sentient Amulet (Very Rare).
While the player character carries the Sentient Amulet, the Cursed Monk occasionally makes comments at various locations and after specific interactions.

name: Shattered Flail

description: Shattered Flail is a rare +2 Mace that heals the wielder when they hit an enemy - at the cost of potentially going mad when they stop attacking.

properties:
Hitting an enemy with this weapon heals the wielder for 1d6Hit Points - but they can go Mad if they don't continue hitting an enemy each turn.
Healing through this item doesn't trigger other passives that react to healing.
Hit an enemy with all your might to deal damage and possibly Daze them. ( Recharge: Short rest.)
where_to_find: The Risen Road X: 33 Y: 597: Carried by Flind, who leads a group of Gnolls in attacking the remaining occupants of the Zhentarim caravan
notes:
After hitting a creature with the Shattered Flail, the wielder gains Yeenoghu's Gift for 6 turns. For the duration, they must succeed a DC 10 Wisdom Saving Throw at the end of any turn on which they do not hit an enemy, or go Mad for 1 turn.
The Saving Throw rolls made by the wielder of this weapon do not appear in the combat log, but they are in fact being rolled at the end of each turn where the wielder does not damage an enemy.
The duration of Yeenoghu's Gift is not refreshed by hitting enemies again; it only lasts the base 6 turns, after which it can be re-applied.

While Mad, the wielder is uncontrollably hostile to all nearby creatures, including allies, and uses any and all tools at their disposal to inflict harm. This could include using powerful Ammunition or Consumables from their inventory, casting high level Spells, or shoving allies to their deaths.

Although the combat log states "Tav healed self...", this healing does not trigger other items which activate on the character's healing such as Boots of Aid and Comfort, The Whispering Promise or Broodmother's Revenge.

The wielder is healed upon each instance of damage. This means that in the case of attacks which deal multiple damage types, such as Booming Blade and Divine Smite (as well as other Smite spells), or in the case of attacks which damage multiple targets, such as Slashing Flourish (Melee), the wielder is healed multiple times.

Voss must be disarmed before beginning the encounter, as he immediately flies away when any hostile action is taken by the party or its allies, and he locks party members into dialogue when they approach close enough.
Due to his high stats, the chance of failing the disarm attempt against him is very high, so this method may require multiple reloads or extensive preparation. See: Guide: Early Silver Sword.

Using Honeyed Paws while having a divination wizard with a 15 or higher portent die nearby guarantees that he drops his weapon. It is possible to long rest until getting 15 or higher and then make the bear invisible. After placing a Potion of Invisibility on the ground, the bear companion can drink it and then approach Voss.

Sometimes, Voss appears with a Githyanki Crossbow instead of the sword or, when dropped, it simply phases out of existence. The triggers for these anomalies are not known. If Voss appears with a crossbow instead of the sword, this Guide explains how to obtain it.

If this sword is obtained in Act One, a second one of this will not be given as a quest reward.
Otherwise, this sword can be acquired in Act Three before entering the Lower City during Deal with the Devil. If the party declines or skips signing the contract with Raphael but successfully lies to Voss, he gives the party the sword ( DC 30 Deception Check).
In addition to Charmed, Githborn Psionic Resistance blocks all (eighteen) conditions in the Charmed status group.

name: Spellcrux Amulet
title: Spellcrux Amulet
description: Spellcrux Amulet is a very rare Amulet that allows the wearer to restore any one spell slot once per Long Rest.
quote: Some scholars have speculated that spells have a mind of their own, suggesting that the spells get bored between being cast and restored.
properties: Replenish an expended spell slot of any level as a Bonus Action once per Long Rest.
where_to_find: Moonrise Towers Prison X: 569 Y: -650: Worn by the Warden
notes: The amulet cannot create new spell slots, only restore used ones. If you do not have a used spell slot of the level you chose, the amulet has no effect.
The amulet can recover spell slots that the caster does not innately have from their class, such as ones gained from Create Spell Slot, or ones from gear, such as Shield of Devotion.
It is capable of recovering both Warlock spell slots and regular spell slots. If you have empty spell slots of both types for the chosen level, it restores one slot for each type.

Likewise, if the amulet is equipped by Gale and he has the Consumed Shadow Weave feature, selecting third level will restore both a normal third-level spell slot and the third-level "shadow spell slot" granted by this feature.

The spell slot is not lost when the amulet is removed, meaning you can put the amulet on, restore a slot, and switch back to another amulet of your choice. The recharge is still tied to the amulet, so this cannot be done with multiple characters at once.

bugs: The in-game description of this passive feature is not entirely correct, and reads as follows:

Instead, creatures Blessed with the Staff of Arcane Blessing gain two separate conditions:
The regular Bless condition, which grants a 1d4 bonus to all saving throws and attack rolls.
The special Mystra's Blessing condition, which grants another 1d4 bonus, but only to spell attack rolls.

Specifically, it is possible to lose the regular Bless condition (due to the caster losing concentration) while retaining the Mystra's Blessing condition. In this case, the creature is left with a 1d4 bonus to spell attack rolls, but loses the other 1d4 bonuses, despite the tooltip of the condition claiming otherwise.
Mystra's Blessing is only applied when Bless is cast using a level 1 or level 2 spell slot, in addition to the once-per-day version granted by the staff itself.

 Bursting Sinew

Life Essence Harvest has no cooldown and can be triggered without limit.
Killing a creature with a spell granted from Life Essence does not provide a new charge of Life Essence.
Indirect spell damage from sources like Spirit Guardians does not provide a charge of Life Essence when killing a hostile creature.

Per the GreaterNecromancySpellFilter() .khn script, this effect is intended to allow the casting of an extra Necromancy spell only if the spell level is equal to or lower than the number of Life Essence turns the wielder has. However, this restriction is currently non-functional, and any level of Necromancy spell can be cast using the effect. Though none of the tooltips explicitly mention this functionality, Life Essence displays the number of turns the wielder has on its tooltip.

description: The Blood of Lathander is a legendary + 3 Mace found through the Find the Blood of Lathander quest. It continuously sheds light, blinds nearby Fiends and Undead with its light, can prevent death as well as heal its wielder, and allows the wielder to cast Sunbeam.

notes: The version of Sunbeam granted by this item does not allow recasting on subsequent turns.

Within the game files, this item has multiple variations with different names, but same functionality:
UUID: 96a35552-0c05-4df0-9974-2a8f142e4be6 (Blood of Lathander). This version of the item has a quote unlike the ingame version, which may have been intended for the usable version: The large chunk of amber set into the handle of this luminous mace supposedly holds four drops of godly blood, fallen to the earth in a battle between an avatar of Lathander and a maddened Chosen of Mystra.
UUID: 7b961f08-46c1-46b1-99bc-c59283831a0b (Dawngrip Mace). This is the current usable variant.

Lathander's Blessing does not activate if the wielder is not in the active party. For example, a companion who is left at camp and receives damage via Warding Bond which reduces their hit points to zero does not cause this effect to trigger.
Lathander's Blessing does not protect against being shoved, thrown, or otherwise forcibly displaced into chasms.
Unlike Light, the Lathander's Light condition works even when wielding a ranged weapon.

The light emitted by Lathander's Light has the following properties:
It does not apply to allies, meaning you won't blind your own summoned undead.
It dispels the Shadow Curse, removing the need to equip a Torch.
It enables effects that require the target be illuminated, such as applying the damage from the Callous Glow Ring.
It is considered sunlight for the purpose of triggering Sunlight Hypersensitivity but is not for Sunlight Sensitivity.
It applies to neutral creatures (including neutral Undead), potentially making them hostile.
bugs:
Lathander's Blessing does not heal allies of the wielder, but rather only active party members nearby.
Due to the way the heal is coded, the attacker who triggered Lathander's Blessing is considered to be the source of the healing. As a result, the healing will not trigger on-heal effects such as Blessed Mercy from The Whispering Promise when equipped by the wielder.
Due to an incorrectly set TargetConditions field, the additional 1d6Hit Points affects the wielder in addition to the 2d6Hit Points.

Due to a timing limitation caused by the method in which healing is applied, the wielder may not always receive all of the healing they are stated to have received in the combat log; they often receive only 1Hit Points (from being stabilized) or 1d6Hit Points, rather than the stated 1d6+2d6Hit Points. It is also possible for the wielder to receive healing, yet still remain dead, showing their lootable corpse with remaining hitpoints.

Due to a missing technical condition (MAG_LATHANDERS_TRACKER) resulting from The Blood of Lathander being spawned in-game via a "Local Item", this passive's "Once per Long Rest" cooldown only refreshes for the wielder during a Long Rest. Equipping the weapon on another character that did not wield the weapon during a Long Rest does not allow this passive to trigger. Additionally, Lathander's Blessing is not reset when consuming a Potion of Angelic Slumber or when affected by Divine Intervention: Opulent Revival.

notes: The Twist of Fortune passive affects all melee damage rolls while equipped, not just damage with Twist of Fortune itself.

This passive stacks with itself (via a second copy of the weapon using the Invoke Duplicity exploit) or by dual wielding with the Knife of the Undermountain King. The damage improvement of the second reroll is smaller than the first one.
If a weapon action misses, using Tenacity does not trigger its effects.

As Tenacity deals weapon damage even if an attack misses, it can trigger many on-hit effects from equipment. For example, from the Gloves of Power, the Callous Glow Ring, weapon coatings, or any infusion from the Ring of Elemental Infusion.

As of Patch 5, this ability consumes gold the target carries in increments of 300 as it is converted to proficiency bonusPiercing damage, so a target with 99,999 gold hit by a level 9 character will have around 99 gold left in their inventory after being dealt approximately [99,900/4]=1330 damage from a hit (before any applicable reductions).
Many bosses and tough enemies in the game can be assassinated with this action by "reverse-pickpocketing" large sums of gold into their inventory.
bugs:
When dual-wielding a flail or morningstar with a non-Tenacity weapon using the Dual Wielder feat, Tenacity can be triggered by missing an attack with the non-Tenacity weapon, dealing Bludgeoning damage regardless of the weapon used.
Some non-Tenacity weapons can trigger their on-hit effects via Tenacity as well, such as the Ritual Dagger and Loviatar's Scourge.

As Horde Breaker (Melee) rolls invisible, zero-damage weapon attacks against all enemies in the Horde Breaker area of effect, Tenacity can be prompted to trigger against them even if the first attack hits. It is therefore possible to score 2 hits in one attack: the full attack against the original Horde Breaker target and a Tenacity hit against another target.
